title: Memory JSON is truncated in place without atomic replacement
evidence: _write_json opens each destination with mode w; no temporary replacement or fsync. crystallize_session writes project, ghosts and system separately at lines 113,129,155.
trigger: Process interruption or write failure after opening a memory file, or between the three writes.
impact: Previously valid memory can become empty/partial, and the three ledgers can disagree; the next read kills the process instead of recovering.

title: Concurrent session consolidation loses completed updates
evidence: Project read-modify-write spans lines 87–113; ghosts and system repeat the same pattern without locking or version checks.
trigger: Two CLI invocations or ledger instances consolidate concurrently after reading the same initial JSON.
impact: The later writer overwrites the other session changes, decisions or session log entries.

title: UTC clock values are mislabeled with a +02:00 offset
evidence: datetime.now(timezone.utc) is formatted with the literal suffix +02:00 without timezone conversion.
trigger: Any call to crystallize_session.
impact: Persisted timestamps represent an instant two hours earlier than the actual event and cannot reliably be correlated with real UTC events.

title: Installer destroys pre-existing agent instruction files without preserving differences
evidence: Lines 168-171 remove any regular .cursorrules/.windsurfrules/.codexrules/CLAUDE.md/.clinerules/.roorules and replace it with a link; lines 179-181 do the same for Copilot. No backup or content preservation occurs. .babylon60rules requires preserving differences before replacing regular files.
trigger: Install Shield in a project with existing custom regular instruction files.
impact: Existing project instructions are irreversibly lost from the working directory.

title: A contender removes an active installer lock after approximately one second
evidence: acquire_lock unconditionally rm -rf removes LOCK_DIR after 200 failed mkdir attempts with sleep 0.005; no owner PID, liveness, or ownership check exists. release_lock also deletes whichever lock currently exists.
trigger: Two installs/uninstalls overlap and the first takes more than the fixed wait interval.
impact: Both processes can enter the critical section and race on global skills, configuration and workspace rules.

title: Uninstall deletes unrelated symlinked instruction files
evidence: The uninstall loop checks only -L and immediately rm -f; unlike installation it never verifies readlink target or an installation ownership manifest.
trigger: Run --uninstall in a project whose CLAUDE.md or other listed instruction file links to a user-maintained source.
impact: The unrelated project instruction link is removed even when Shield did not create it.

title: Persistent retry deadlines use a clock that resets at reboot
evidence: Worker compares next_retry_at to time.monotonic at 43-54 and stores it at 77; producer pulmones.py:87 stores time.monotonic()+delay in SQLite.
trigger: Reboot after queueing a task when the previous uptime was long.
impact: Persisted deadlines remain in the previous boot clock domain and can postpone retries for the old uptime duration.

title: Fetching retry work does not claim rows atomically
evidence: SELECT at 46-55 has no lease/status update; execution happens at 110 and deletion only at 113 via a separate connection.
trigger: Run two PulmonesWorker processes on the same database and fetch the same ripe batch before either deletes it.
impact: Both workers execute the same queued side effect; there is no ownership claim or deduplication in this worker.

title: Remove globally inconsistent list-length axiom from generated Lean
evidence: Generated anergy_purge_limit quantifies over every List OncologyPrimitive and asserts length > 300 implies False; a list repeating any constructible OncologyPrimitive 301 times contradicts it.
trigger: Import/use the generated axiom in formal reasoning.
impact: False becomes derivable; downstream propositions using the axiom cannot establish the intended guarantee. This is a proof issue, not runtime containment evidence.

title: Close the namespace in generated Lean output
evidence: The template opens namespace Babylon60.Oncology, then writes the generated file after the last axiom without an end declaration.
trigger: Export Lean from this generator.
impact: Generated source has an unclosed namespace and cannot complete clean Lean compilation. No compiler was run.

title: Do not unlink SQLite journals based solely on their suffix
evidence: run_cohort_1 unlinks every .db-wal/.db-shm under WORKSPACE and CORTEX_DIR; no connection, checkpoint, liveness or orphan check precedes unlink. main invokes it unconditionally.
trigger: Run this purge while a non-protected SQLite database has committed WAL pages not checkpointed into the main file.
impact: The script can remove durable committed pages and disrupt active database coordination; the comment calling these files orphans does not establish that they are orphaned.

title: Limit Lean cleanup to verified disposable build products
evidence: The comment scopes cleanup to obsolete caches in archived projects, but traversal covers all WORKSPACE and rmtree removes the complete .lake directory without archive/state checks.
trigger: Run the script with an active unprotected Lean project under ~/10_PROJECTS.
impact: Deletes active fetched dependencies and any local changes under .lake/packages, and removes artifacts needed by subsequent verification. The implementation does not enforce its stated archived-only scope.

title: Signed integer division can panic instead of returning Critical halt
evidence: Div checks rhs == 0 only, then evaluates lhs / rhs. LoadImm accepts every i64, including i64::MIN.
trigger: LoadImm R1 i64::MIN followed by Div R1 -1.
impact: Signed division overflow panics, violating step's documented no-panic transition contract; callers cannot handle this through HaltReason.

title: Zero-copy PoC reports success after dropped-message timeout
evidence: The receive-count timeout breaks at 94-96; line 109 unconditionally prints FALSACION EMPIRICA SUPERADA. No final equality assertion or failing exit.
trigger: Subscriber receives fewer than msg_count before timeout, or its receive loop exits on error.
impact: PoC exits successfully and advertises empirical success despite incomplete delivery; allocation-free claims are also not measured here.

title: Queued claims capture an obsolete predecessor and are silently discarded
evidence: ingest_entropy snapshots self._last_hash before enqueue; prev_hash is UNIQUE (line 63). _process_claim treats every IntegrityError as replay and _verify_idempotency_collision accepts an absent claim_id.
trigger: Enqueue two different claims before the first INSERT completes. Both contain the same prev_hash; only the first INSERT succeeds.
impact: The second accepted tracking ID is reported as legitimate replay despite never being persisted. Assign predecessor at serialized processing and discriminate constraint collisions.

title: Unescaped description can break generated Python source
evidence: contract.description is interpolated directly into a triple-double-quoted function docstring; McpCandidateContract is an unconstrained dataclass and deduce_contract accepts custom_description.
trigger: A valid description includes a triple-double-quote sequence.
impact: Scaffolding succeeds and persists a syntactically invalid server artifact; later initialization fails. No claim of execution-authorization bypass is made.

title: Counterexample learning returns success without persisting feedback
evidence: The public learn_from_failure function promises persistence in its docstring (18), but its entire implementation is logger.info followed by return True (20-21); it is re-exported by verification/__init__.py.
trigger: A caller invokes learn_from_failure with a verification counterexample expecting the documented durable feedback.
impact: The caller receives success although no cortex memory operation occurs; feedback disappears when logging is disabled or logs expire. No active production caller was established.

title: Normalize rational ticks before returning them
evidence: from_rational constructs Tick60 directly with seconds unchanged and sexa_units=num*factor, while new normalizes units and sub/derived ordering rely on normalized seconds.
trigger: Tick60::from_rational(0, 60, 60) produces (0,FRACTION_BASE), whereas Tick60::new(1,0) produces (1,0).
impact: Equivalent durations compare unequal and sub of the former minus the latter incorrectly returns underflow. Use the normalizing constructor and define overflow handling.

title: TOCTOU harness can certify a campaign that performs no attack
evidence: Attack turns occur only when iter % 3 != 0 (198). pass at 399-402 checks intact victim, zero victim damage and any authorized operation, but does not require an attack attempt or security_aborts > 0, although the header lists that as a pass criterion (23).
trigger: Invoke the example with --workers 1 --iterations 1: the only iteration is iter=0 and therefore never swaps the target.
impact: A clean operation can produce SUPPORTED_WITHIN_DOMAIN and exit 0 without exercising the intended adversarial containment, weakening the evidence claimed by this example.

title: Vault consolidation records a fixed session catalogue instead of reading source sessions
evidence: REPORT_PATH and REPORT_FALLBACK are declared but never read; the loop inserts the static UNCONSOLIDATED_SESSIONS into L1/L3 and vault_consolidations, commits at 212, and reports SUCCESS at 224.
trigger: Running consolidation against an empty vault or with source logs missing or differing from the embedded catalogue.
impact: Persistent memory is populated with summaries and consolidation attestations without evidence that those sessions exist or were actually consolidated; subsequent runs skip those IDs.

title: Failover demo reports success when every tier is unavailable
evidence: When t1_alive, t2_alive and t3_alive are all false, delegated mode enters the failure branch but falls through to RESOLVED/Tier1:Antigravity.
trigger: execute_request(MockGatewayState(t1_alive=False,t2_alive=False,t3_alive=False),...) with delegate_to_kernel=True.
impact: The demonstration counts a failed request as resolved and cannot support its failover reliability claim for total outage.

title: History rewrite discards local work before establishing backup
evidence: _ensure_main executes checkout main then reset --hard origin/main; main calls it first (90). No clean-tree check or backup creation exists although header claims preservation.
trigger: Operator runs script with uncommitted main changes or local main commits ahead of origin/main.
impact: Tracked work and local main history are discarded before rewrite validation. This is direct CLI behavior, not inferred downstream execution.

title: Stale lock eviction can delete a live replacement lock
evidence: exists/getmtime/unlink occur separately; eviction uses age alone, with no owner or inode validation; release_lock unlinks any existing lock.
trigger: Two contenders observe an old lock; one removes it and acquires a new lock before the other performs its already-planned unlink. A live operation longer than 300 seconds is another eviction trigger.
impact: Both processes may believe they own the workspace mutation lock. No mutation consumer was found in targeted scripts/tests search; scope is correctness of the helper itself.

title: Registry verification succeeds despite stale entries and metadata drift
evidence: sync_skills_json removes purged_skills from entry_map and recomputes metadata, aliases, adjacency and audit vectors, but verify_only returns only len(missing)==0 without comparing the recomputed data with the loaded registry. CLI propagates this boolean to the exit status at line 523.
trigger: Remove an obsolete physical skill or change an existing skill's role/alias while every remaining physical skill already has an entry, then use --verify.
impact: Verification can exit zero while docs/skills.json still contains ghost entries or stale routing metadata. Static control-flow finding; no verifier was executed.

title: Batch audit hardcodes successful falsification verdicts
evidence: Keyword branches assign only SURVIVE; scores use line counts/type-token ratios and number of preassigned SURVIVE labels. Generated report states POPPERIAN_SURVIVED and invariants checked without a falsification operation.
trigger: Run the script on any matching Markdown posts.
impact: It generates purported forensic validation and physical/causal scores unsupported by its computations; this is report-generation behavior, not evidence of the underlying claims.

title: FIFO lifecycle test deletes the native host shared queue
evidence: Test imports production QUEUE_FILE then unlinks it at lines 104 and 120 without monkeypatching. scripts/c5_cli/moskv_native_host.py:181 sets QUEUE_FILE=/tmp/moskv_fx_queue.json.
trigger: Run this unit test while the native messaging host has queued prompts.
impact: Queued user work is deleted and the test mutates shared live state; parallel tests or host operations can interfere.

title: TURN credential example accepts any nonempty Authorization header
evidence: Basic Worker example checks only header presence at 83-86 then requests and returns TURN relay credentials at 88-120. No token validation occurs in the complete example.
trigger: Deploying the example and requesting /turn-credentials with an arbitrary Authorization value.
impact: Unauthenticated clients can obtain relay credentials and consume relay quota in deployments copied from this example. No deployed endpoint was identified.

title: New face tracks are returned twice on their first frame
evidence: New track is appended to assignments at 267-268 but never added to matched_tracks; the lost-track loop at 272-276 immediately increments lost and appends it again. c5_face_swap_cli.py:368-372 consumes update and :396 iterates every assignment.
trigger: A detected face has no existing matching track and is assigned an identity with default max_extrapolate=2.
impact: Face-swap processing runs twice for the same face on its initial frame, adds redundant inference/compositing, and incorrectly marks a new track as lost.

title: Use a unique temporary audio file for each synthesis
evidence: Each invocation writes /tmp/f5_raw_synthesis.wav before launching ffmpeg against that same path; no exclusive creation, per-run directory or cleanup protects it.
trigger: Two syntheses overlap after one writes its audio and before its ffmpeg has read it.
impact: An output may contain another synthesis audio, or a concurrent write may corrupt conversion; the fixed file also retains synthesized speech.
